issues.title: No absolute scroll positioning — 'scroll to top/bottom' missing

sections.body: Try to scroll back to the top of a page after scrolling down. `scroll up 99999` works but is imprecise; `scroll top` is not a command.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A built-in way to scroll to absolute positions (top, bottom, or a specific pixel offset from top) without needing JavaScript eval.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The `scroll` command only supports relative offsets (`scroll up/down/left/right <pixels>`). Scrolling to top requires `eval "window.scrollTo(0, 0)"` — a JavaScript escape hatch that a non-technical user wouldn't know.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The `scroll` command was designed for incremental scrolling only. No `scroll-top`, `scroll-bottom`, or absolute position target was implemented.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands/scroll.rs or where scroll command is defined
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add `scroll top` and `scroll bottom` subcommands for absolute positioning
- Alternatively, accept `scroll to <pixels>` for absolute scroll-to-position
- Document the eval workaround in the scroll help text until the feature is added
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Scroll output lacks page height context

sections.body: Run `scroll down 800`. Output: `Scrolled down 800px (position: 800.0)`.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Output should include total page height so the user knows progress: e.g., `Scrolled down 800px (position: 800 / 8500, 9%)`.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Only shows the new scroll position without total page height. User cannot gauge how far through the page they are.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The scroll command output formatter doesn't query `document.body.scrollHeight` or equivalent to compute total page height.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Include total page height in scroll output (e.g., `position: 800/7200px (11%)`)
- This small change dramatically improves the UX of long-page scrolling
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Session reuse message could confuse first-time users

sections.body: Run `goto` when a DEFAULT session already exists. Output begins with `Using existing session DEFAULT (current page: ...)`.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either a clean new session or a clear prompt/option to choose between reusing and refreshing.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The session was transparently reused. While convenient, a first-time user might not understand what 'DEFAULT session' means, why there's already a page loaded, or whether this affects the task.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Auto-session-reuse is the default behavior of `goto`. The message `Using existing session DEFAULT` is informational but assumes familiarity with the session model.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a brief explanation on first run: 'Sessions persist between commands. Use `close` to end a session.'
- Consider `goto --fresh` flag to force a new window
- Add session state indicator (clean vs. reused) to the output
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No `--stdout` or pipe support for screenshot command

sections.body: There is no `--stdout` flag on the `screenshot` command. Screenshots always write to a file.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A `--stdout` flag or pipe support to stream screenshot data, useful for chaining with image processing tools.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Screenshots must always go to a file. For quick inspection, the user must open the file separately.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The screenshot command was designed as a file-output-only operation. Streaming binary data to stdout may have been deprioritized.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add `--stdout` flag to emit PNG data to stdout (similar to `snapshot --stdout`)
- This enables `browser4-cli screenshot --stdout | feh -` and similar pipelines
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Snapshot auto-generated on `goto` but path format is noisy

sections.body: Run `goto <url>`. Output includes `[Snapshot](/home/vincent/workspace/Browser4-4.12/.browser4-cli/snapshot/snapshot-2026-07-28T03-03-45-172Z.yml)`.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The snapshot path should use a relative or shortened format in the terminal output for readability, especially since the full absolute path is long.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The full absolute filesystem path is printed, which is noisy in terminal output (116 characters for the path alone).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The output formatter uses the absolute path. No relative-path or tilde-shortening is applied.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Use `~` shorthand for paths under the home directory
- Or show paths relative to the repo root when inside it
- Keep the full path accessible via a `--verbose` flag
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `screenshot --filename` help doesn't explain where 'snapshot directory' is

sections.body: Run `screenshot --help`. It says 'Bare filenames are saved to the snapshot directory' but doesn't say what or where that directory is.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The help should state the snapshot directory's default path (e.g., `~/.browser4-cli/snapshot/`) or how to discover it.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A new user must guess or learn from other output messages that the snapshot directory is `.browser4-cli/snapshot/` under the working directory.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The help text assumes the user already knows the snapshot directory location from prior context.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add the default snapshot directory path to the `--filename` help text
- Or add a `browser4-cli config` command that shows paths
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No `snapshot -i` option flow guidance in help text

sections.body: A new user reading the help output sees `snapshot` with flags like `-v N`, `-i`, `--auto-diff` but no explanation of when to use which mode.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Brief guidance on when to use interactive vs. viewport-based snapshots.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The help output lists flags tersely: `-v N` for viewport chunks, `-i` for interactive, `--auto-diff` for diffs. A new user must consult SKILL.md for context.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI help is intentionally brief, with detailed guidance in SKILL.md. However, new users may not know SKILL.md exists.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a reference to SKILL.md in the `snapshot --help` output
- Or add a one-line description of when to use each snapshot mode
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `wait` numeric target vs. text target ambiguity could cause confusion

sections.body: `wait 2000` waits 2 seconds (time). `wait e1` waits for element (selector). `wait Architecture` — would this wait for text 'Architecture' or try to match an element?
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clear documentation of positional argument disambiguation rules.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The docs say 'interpreted as milliseconds when numeric, otherwise as a CSS selector or element ref'. It's unclear what happens with a non-numeric string that's also a CSS selector.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The positional argument has dual semantics (time vs. selector). Non-numeric strings that aren't valid CSS selectors may fail confusingly.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add an explicit example showing the `wait --text` form is preferred for text matching
- Consider warning when a non-numeric string isn't a valid CSS selector or ref
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
